question: When an AI tool makes a quick choice for us, how do we know when to trust it and when to ask a person?
reflection: Tools that say how sure they are can help people focus their care on the hard cases, where human judgement matters most.

sources.subject: System One models are carving out a new layer in the AI stack

one_line: A new kind of small AI model that picks from fixed options, instead of writing text, promises much cheaper and faster decisions.

top_stories.title: Decision models that choose instead of write
top_stories.what: A startup released Jev, a model that returns a choice from options you define, with a confidence score, and reportedly costs far less than a full language model for such tasks.
top_stories.why: Sorting survey answers, complaints or support requests into set categories could become cheap and measurable, with unsure cases sent to people.

top_stories.title: Open alternatives appear quickly
top_stories.what: An open-source model called Laya and a research model called CLM-8B take similar approaches, and the researchers report CLM ran faster in their own tests.
top_stories.why: Open options let teams run such classifiers on their own servers, which helps when data must stay in the country.

saudi_lens.text: No direct Saudi link today, though self-hosted decision models could help agencies sort Arabic citizen feedback while keeping data inside the Kingdom.

idea.title: Confidence-based feedback triage
idea.pitch: Pilot a small decision model that sorts public feedback into categories, auto-routes confident cases and sends uncertain ones to staff.
idea.first_step: Write a clear, complete list of categories for one feedback channel and label 100 past messages by hand.

idea_kids.title: How sure are you? sorting game
idea_kids.pitch: Children sort picture cards into boxes and hold up a number from one to five showing how sure they feel, then discuss the unsure ones together.
idea_kids.first_step: Prepare thirty picture cards, including a few that could fit in two boxes.

watchlist.name: TypeSafe AI
watchlist.note: Its Jev model started a new class of low-cost decision models.

tool.name: Laya
tool.use: Open-source model that picks or scores answers from a list you define, and can run on modest hardware.

verify: TypeSafe claims Jev is 40 to 200 times faster than frontier models for decision tasks.
TypeSafe claims cost savings of over 400 times for such tasks.

terms.definition: A model that writes its output one piece at a time, each piece based on what came before.
When a model's stated certainty matches how often it is actually right.
Using one AI model to score or check the answers produced by another.

concepts.summary: Small models built only to choose, score or rank, at a fraction of the cost of general models.
Fast classifiers sort open text into categories and flag uncertain cases for people.
